438392eaf0a3a301: SINGAPORE, Sept 29 — A 30-year-old man is due to be charged in court today after an AI-generated image of a crocodile he created triggered a search operation at and the suspension of water activities there.
CNA reported that the man allegedly created the image and sent it to a colleague, prompting authorities to act after a crocodile sighting was reported at the reservoir on August 20.
The national water agency PUB subsequently advised members of the public to exercise caution, while its personnel and the National Parks Board carried out searches for the reptile.
The image was later determined to be fabricated, prompting a police report the following day.
Police said preliminary investigations found that the man had created the AI-generated image before sending it to his colleague.
The man later deleted both the image and the application used to create it, which police said was an attempt to conceal his actions.
He is expected to face charges of communicating a false message and obstructing the course of justice.
A conviction for communicating a false message carries a maximum jail term of three years, a fine of up to S$10,000 (RM32,000), or both.
Those convicted of obstructing the course of justice can be jailed for up to seven years, fined, or both.
Police said false information could cause public alarm while diverting government resources towards incidents that did not occur.
They urged the public not to circulate false information or manipulated images that could unnecessarily alarm others.
Police also warned against submitting fabricated or digitally altered material, including AI-generated images, to authorities while representing it as genuine.
42e751125c014406: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians who withdraw their retirement savings in a lump sum risk missing out on further compounding gains that could help their money last longer, said Finance Minister II.
Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said regular monthly withdrawals would allow the remaining savings to stay invested and continue compounding, helping retirees stretch their funds over a longer period.

"Taking money out through monthly withdrawals, rather than as a lump sum, allows the funds to continue compounding and helps retirees' savings last longer," he said on the sidelines of the EPF International Social Wellbeing Conference 2026.
"This gives people a clearer picture of their retirement income and what they can do to improve their financial position going forward," he said.
Amir said the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) had introduced new tools to help members understand how different withdrawal patterns could affect their retirement income.

Among them is the Retirement Goal Calculator, a digital planning tool that allows members to set their desired monthly retirement income and assess whether their savings are sufficient to meet that target.
He said giving members a clearer picture of their potential monthly retirement income could help them make more informed decisions about when and how much to withdraw.
"The new tool allows members to plan for their retirement through the app, including setting the amount they want to withdraw each month after retirement.
"This gives people a clearer picture of their retirement income and what they can do to improve their financial position going forward," he said.
Amir said EPF's Retirement Income Adequacy framework also provides different savings thresholds based on members' desired retirement lifestyles.
The framework includes an automatic adjustment mechanism to account for inflation, ensuring savings targets keep pace with changes in living costs.
He said clearer savings targets and practical planning tools would help members make informed financial decisions about their retirement.
d99388196f683a80: HONG KONG, Sept 29 — Shares in Chinese fast-fashion giant Shein plunged more than 11 per cent in Hong Kong on Tuesday after releasing disappointing financial results.

The company has faced scrutiny over its environmental footprint and allegations of human rights violations, and faces growing competition from low-cost e-commerce companies such as Temu and AliExpress.
The firm said on Monday that revenue grew just one per cent on-year in the first six months of the year, while its operating profit halved.
By around lunch on Tuesday, Shein’s share price had pared some of the losses but was still down 10.9 per cent at HK$31.44 (RM16.36).

Monday’s results were Shein’s first since its high-profile initial public offering this month, which put the company’s valuation at around US$26.3 billion — well short of the nearly US$100 billion during private fundraising rounds in 2022.
Net revenue from Europe fell 13.9 per cent to nearly US$3.8 billion for the second quarter, Shein reported.
The decrease “reflects a decline in sales volume as we raised prices and lowered online advertising spending” in anticipation of the removal of the customs duty exemption, the company said.
Another key market, the United States, saw revenue drop six per cent in April-June, reflecting the impact of tariffs.
Since its first day of trading on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in September, Shein’s share price has fallen more than 35 per cent.

The accelerating decline in Shein’s operating profit “clouds the extent of a 2027 recovery from freight relief and an unproven push into higher-priced brands”, said Catherine Lim, an analyst at Business Intelligence.

“Management plans to absorb freight and tariff costs rather than raise prices to protect the company’s competitive position,” she said, adding that localising stock in Europe will lead to higher logistics costs in the short term. — AFP
c98826dcf0176558: SHAH ALAM: The High Court here today found the government liable for losses suffered by residents of Taman Sri Muda during the devastating December 2021 floods.
The ruling came in a suit filed by 50 residents who accused the authorities of negligence and breaches of duty in their handling of the disaster.
Senior federal counsel Liew Horng Bin, when asked whether the government would appeal the ruling, said he was not in a position to comment at the moment.
The residents had sued the government and nine others, claiming that failures in flood management, drainage, weather warnings and disaster response had contributed to the losses they suffered.
They are seeking RM3,767,148.51 in special damages, as well as general and aggravated damages.
b69513cd01e29cba: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — Applications for the government's medicine delivery service (UMP) should be done only through the Ministry of Health, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today as he cautioned against possible scam attempts.
"Registration for the UMP programme is only conducted through KKM facilities, not via TikTok or Facebook accounts," the minister told reporters after launching the initiative here.
"I remind everyone there is no registration process other than at health clinics or Ministry of Health facilities only."

Patients in Malaysia will soon be able to receive their follow-up medication delivered directly to their doorstep free of charge, following a joint funding initiative announced today by the Communications Ministry and the Health Ministry.
Starting Oct 1, eligible patients will enjoy fully subsidized shipping costs for their follow-up prescriptions for a duration of one year under the UMP programme.

"The initiative is introduced to encourage more patients to utilise digital healthcare services, while simultaneously improving access to follow-up medications without requiring them to physically visit health facilities," the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) said in a statement today.
Fahmi encouraged the public to seek more information, reiterating that registration for the programme is free.
"Registration for the UMP program is free and does not require any payment," he said.

Under the strategic partnership, the MCMC — acting in its capacity as the regulator of the country's postal sector — will coordinate the execution of the programme, while the MOH will manage patient eligibility and medication supply.
The physical delivery of the medications will be handled by Pos Malaysia Berhad.
The programme could benefit some 80,000 patients across the country each month, with estimated total shipping subsidy of RM5 million.
258ce096763a8e40: NAGOYA: Rain continued to disrupt the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Tuesday, with Sri Lanka and Bangladesh advancing to the men's cricket semi-finals after their quarter-final matches were abandoned without a ball being bowled.

Sri Lanka had been scheduled to face Nepal, while Bangladesh were set to take on Malaysia. However, a second consecutive day of no play at the Korogi Sports Park, on the southern outskirts of Nagoya, meant the higher-ranked teams progressed automatically to the last four.
Jarrad Shearer, the games' sports director,could not hide his disappointment after organisers spent an entire year converting a baseball diamond into a cricket venue, only to see minimal action.
"Cricket, like baseball, you can't play it in the rain. A year of my life on this, and it rains," Shearer said.
Sri Lanka will now take on defending champions India, while Bangladesh face Pakistan in the semi-finals on Thursday.
Bangladesh will be without Najmul Hossain Shanto, however, after the batter was ruled out of the tournament due to a fever and infection.
Despite the washouts, Shearer remained optimistic the weather would clear in time for the top-tier cricket.
"Come tomorrow morning it will be all hands on deck to dry up the areas that aren't under the covers. We've got some soppers, we've got some squeegees, some big old brooms, we've got sponges.
"Plus, it's supposed to be sunny and 32 C (89.6 Fahrenheit), so with any luck we'll soak up as much water as we can in the morning and the sun will do its work in the afternoon." --REUTERS
0b35ce9d04c8a04d: JAKARTA, Sept 29 — Malaysia are ready to take on Singapore in their final Fifa Asean Cup 2026 Division 1 Group A match in Bandung this Thursday despite a demanding turnaround, says interim head coach Tan Cheng Hoe.

Cheng Hoe said the Harimau Malaya had gained valuable confidence and experience from their two opening matches, including last night’s goalless draw with hosts Indonesia at Gelora Bung Karno (GBK) Stadium here.
However, he expects another stern test when Malaysia face Singapore at Stadium Si Jalak Harupat, with the race for a place in the final still wide open.
“I think our players gained experience, confidence and so many moments as a team. We still have a tough game playing against Singapore, as we said, it is a Causeway derby.

“We know playing against Singapore will be another tough match, but I’m sure after getting this good result against Indonesia, we are ready,” he told a post-match press conference after Malaysia’s 0-0 draw with Indonesia.
The 58-year-old coach said recovery and preparation would be crucial for Malaysia after two physically demanding matches and a journey to Bandung.

“We have a a tough time also, we have to travel to Bandung. It’s not an excuse but sometimes in football, you need a good recovery, good preparation and we are ready to play against Singapore,” he said.
The former Kedah and Selangor FC coach said the technical staff would assess the players’ fitness before deciding on the best starting line-up and any changes for the Singapore clash.

Meanwhile, on the understanding displayed by Johor Darul Ta’zim (JDT) players in the national side, Cheng Hoe said their established chemistry provided an advantage but stressed that Malaysia’s success depended on a collective performance.
“The chemistry and understanding of the JDT players give us an advantage, but football requires us to play as a team, not only JDT players. I focus on the team performance,” he said.
Malaysia lead Group A with four points, level with second-placed Indonesia but ahead on goal difference, while Singapore are third on three points and Bangladesh remain bottom without a point.

In the inaugural tournament, the group winners will advance to the final, while the runners-up will contest the third-place playoff, with both matches scheduled to be held at GBK next Monday. — Bernama
9c0b32139c24ba2e: JAKARTA, Sept 29 — Malaysia captain Dion Cools admitted he was disappointed that Harimau Malaya could not leave Gelora Bung Karno (GBK) Stadium here with all three points after their goalless Fifa Asean Cup 2026 Division 1 Group A draw with Indonesia, last night.

Cools said Malaysia were particularly dominant in the second half and deserved more from the contest against the hosts, who had been reduced to 10 men for about 70 minutes after midfielder Thom Haye was shown a red card.

However, the Cerezo Osaka FC defender stressed that the point earned would count for little unless Malaysia produce the required result against Singapore in their final group match at Si Jalak Harupat Stadium in Bandung on Thursday.

“Very proud of the performance but at the same time a little disappointed in the result. I guess we were quite dominant, especially second half. We wished to have the three points to go home but unfortunately, it’s only one point but everything is still open.

“Next game, we just have to put a good result down against Singapore. We know it will be very tough, but we are confident we can do it, so we need to prepare very well, recover very well, and then there’s a big chance we can play the final,” he told reporters after Malaysia’s 0-0 draw with Indonesia.
The 30-year-old said Malaysia must respect Singapore but remain confident in their own strengths as they pursue the goals needed to remain in the race for a place in the final.

“On paper that’s of course the idea (to score as many goals as possible) but we know Singapore is a really tough opponent, so we need to be very respectful but at the same time, we need to go on from our own strength.
“We need to get some confidence from today (last night) and keep going, and hopefully next game we can score some goals and secure our final spot in the final,” he said.
Cools said recovery would be key in the short turnaround before the team travel to Bandung.
Malaysia currently lead Group A with four points, level with Indonesia but ahead on goal difference, while Singapore are third on three points and Bangladesh remain bottom without a point.

In the inaugural tournament, the group winners will advance to the final, while the runners-up will contest the third-place playoff, with both matches scheduled to be held at GBK next Monday. — Bernama
6529cafe89c44b28: KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry is expanding closed-circuit television (CCTV) coverage to 333 boarding schools this year, with an additional RM5 million allocation, as part of efforts to strengthen student safety and curb bullying.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said 300 MySTEP warden assistants were also deployed from April to help monitor students in hostels, particularly at night.
"I understand the anxiety parents feel whenever a bullying incident occurs. I am a mother, too. My own child studied and lived in a hostel within the same education system.

"There are measures we initiated several years ago, and there are also new measures introduced after recognising that there is still room for improvement," she said in a Facebook post outlining the ministry's efforts to address bullying in schools.

She said the ministry's bullying complaint system had also been enhanced with an anonymous reporting function through the MOE Bullying Complaint Portal to protect the identities of complainants and witnesses.

Prevention and early intervention efforts have also been strengthened through the S.A.F.E. Framework, which covers prevention, early intervention and rehabilitation, including Peer Support Groups and targeted counselling.
Fadhlina said Character Education would be introduced in the 2027 School Curriculum, with an emphasis on values such as integrity and empathy.

She said the ministry was also working with the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department to draft the Anti-Bullying Act 2026, which would include provisions for an Anti-Bullying Tribunal as a channel for victims to seek redress.

"The ministry also introduced the Guidelines on Managing Bullying Misconduct in 2023 as an official reference for schools in receiving complaints, conducting investigations, taking disciplinary action and implementing interventions," she said.
Fadhlina stressed that the ministry must not be complacent and would continue evaluating and addressing shortcomings as long as students felt unsafe at school.
"As long as there is a child who does not feel safe at school, our work is not yet done," she said.

4a1413f349d86303: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is offering training to 100 young Malaysians to pursue careers as seafarers under the Armada Madani programme.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the programme involves a RM10 million allocation from the Malaysia Shipping Development Fund (MSDF), with priority given to those from B40 households.
"Malaysia's maritime future depends on the people who will sail our ships and sustain our shipping industry.

"Through the Armada Madani Programme, the government is investing RM10 million from the MSDF to help 100 young Malaysians, particularly those from B40 households, pursue careers as seafarers," he said in his speech at the 2026 Malaysia Maritime Week today.
Loke said the programme offered two pathways for those who had completed the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia or an equivalent qualification.
He said 50 students would undertake three-year diploma programmes in Nautical Studies or Marine Engineering, with RM120,000 allocated per student.
Loke said another 50 would receive six months of training as Deck Ratings or Engine Ratings, with RM15,000 allocated per student.
On the MSDF, Loke said the fund, established under the recently enacted A1551 legislation, would serve as a strategic financial mechanism to strengthen domestic shipping capacity.
He said it was designed to empower local operators, expand the Malaysian-flagged fleet and ensure a greater share of the nation's trade remained supported by domestic shipping capacity.
ecf603508f52762f: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission yesterday detained a former senior management officer of a corporation over the alleged misuse of position involving operating expenditure payments worth RM42 million.
The arrest is believed to be linked to an ongoing investigation into millions of ringgit in losses suffered by UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd (UiTM Holdings) in 2023.
The man, aged in his 50s, was arrested at 1pm at his residence in the Klang Valley.
Preliminary investigations found that the former senior officer had allegedly abused his position in 2017 by approving or making operational payments to several companies.
Investigators also found that he had direct personal interests in companies that received the funds, which amounted to millions of ringgit.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrest when contacted.
He said an investigation paper had been opened and the case was being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009 for using office or position for gratification.
"The suspect is expected to be charged in court this Thursday," he said.
UiTM Holdings, a wholly owned investment arm of Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM), came under public scrutiny in early 2023 following reports of substantial losses.

Reports at the time said the public university's subsidiary had recorded accumulated losses amounting to millions of ringgit over four consecutive years, raising concerns over the governance and management of Bumiputera investment funds.

Following the disclosures, MACC launched a comprehensive investigation into financial documents, investment transactions and the company's corporate profile to determine whether there had been leakages, misappropriation or abuse of power by its senior management.
bc8330514cbef8d6: NAGOYA: Debutant Ke Qun Tao is eyeing a comeback in the lead event later this week after finishing 14th in the men's boulder semi-finals at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games today.
Qun Tao admitted he struggled with nerves in the boulder discipline.
He was unable to top the first three boulders but scored 24.7 on the final boulder at the Portmesse Nagoya Exhibition Hall.
South Korea's Lee Dohyun (99.7), Japan's Sorata Anraku (99.3) and China's Pan Yufei (84.1) took the top three spots.
Only the top eight climbers from the 15 semi-finalists advanced to tomorrow's final.
"This is my first Asian Games so I was really nervous, I felt like I couldn't get a proper warm up," he said.
"I couldn't think straight for the first two minutes on the first boulder. When I finally started to find the correct way, I couldn't keep it together and I was a bit too tired to finish it.
"So when I finally topped the last boulder, it was like a breath of fresh air. I finally felt that I could perform like I usually do.

"What I can take away from today is that the pressure of the Asian Games is immense. I think I was really focused on the technicalities of climbing, like movement and strength, but I did not pay enough attention to the mindset and pressure aspect."
The 21-year-old is now looking ahead to the lead event semi-finals on Friday, which is his favoured discipline.
"The lead event is actually my favourite, I qualified for lead first and only realised I qualified for boulder about two months ago, so my training has been mainly focused on lead," he said.
"I don't think I will be more relaxed but I will definitely have more of an idea of how the situation feels like. I will do my best to prepare mentally and deliver my best performance."
Melbourne-based Qun Tao is competing in Nagoya under the Olympic Council of Malaysia's category B classification and is self-funded, though he will be reimbursed by the government if he wins a medal.
He is currently studying commerce at the University of Melbourne.
baacbef9debdc0cf: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim extended his heartfelt congratulations to the Sultan of Kelantan, Sultan Muhammad V, on the occasion of the ruler’s 57th birthday.
In a Facebook post today, Anwar prayed that Sultan Muhammad V and the entire royal family will always be blessed with His grace and guidance.
“May Allah protect Tuanku in this world and the hereafter. Daulat Tuanku,” he said. — Bernama

da0667dc6e0abece: NEW YORK, Sept 29 — US air safety regulators are delaying certification of the 737 MAX 10 until determining a fresh software glitch poses no safety risk, a top official said Monday.
The problem stems from a cockpit software update to the 737 MAX that can cause an automated navigation feature to fail when planes shift their approach to landing.
Shares of Boeing, which has staked its turnaround in part of MAX production growth, fell sharply Monday after a weekend Wall Street Journal article outlined the problem.

While pilots are trained to safely land planes without the automated navigation system, regulators must evaluate whether the “workload” is excessive for pilots under such a scenario, said FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford.
Bedford said Monday at a press conference that the MAX planes certified by FAA thus far are safe but that “we will be delaying the 10 until... we’re satisfied we don’t have an issue here.”

Earlier, an FAA spokesperson said the regulator “is working closely with Boeing and the airlines,” adding that the FAA will convene an advisory board and “will take immediate action if it identifies a safety concern.”

The statements come after Boeing Chief Executive Officer Kelly Ortberg told a Wall Street conference on September 16 that he expected Federal Aviation Administration certification of the 737 MAX 10 “very soon.”
A Boeing spokesperson said Monday that, “we continue to follow the lead of the FAA as we work through the certification process.”
The problem surfaces when pilots alter their preprogrammed flight plan following a missed approach, according to Boeing.

“Last month, we informed all 737 operators about a software issue where pilots may not have access to automated flight guidance during a specific landing scenario,” a Boeing spokesperson said Monday in an emailed statement.
“We shared information with operators that reinforced existing pilot procedures for safely handling such cases.”
Boeing engineers “are working on a software update to permanently address the issue,” the spokesperson said.
Boeing’s woes
Boeing has staked its corporate turnaround in part on growth of 737 MAX production. The aircraft was grounded for 20 months through November 2020 following fatal MAX crashes in 2018 and 2019.
Airlines have been eager to receive the 737 MAX 10, which, like other Boeing jets, has been heavily delayed by the company’s safety problems.
The FAA certified the smaller, long-delayed 737 MAX 7 on August 3.

Bedford said the 737 MAX 7 is “safe” to fly, describing the software issue as akin to an update for iPhone or a Microsoft product. In this instance, Boeing “fixed a known bug” but introduced “a new bug, smaller.”
Bedford described the issue as very different from the flaw that led to the two deadly MAX crashes.
In those cases, a poorly conceived flight navigation system known as the Maneuvering Characteristics Augmentation System (MCAS) took control of the aircraft.
“The pilots remain in control of the airplane,” Bedford said of the new software defect. “They train for these scenarios.”
Three major MAX buyers told AFP they don’t fly planes with the problematic new version of the flight management computer software.
“United does not currently have any 737s operating with this new FMC software, and we are not taking deliveries of new aircraft with the new FMC software,” United said.

Southwest Airlines “is aware of the issue and is engaged with Boeing and the FAA,” said a spokesperson for the carrier who added that all newly delivered planes have older software versions installed.

“We have been engaged with Boeing and the FAA and will continue to work closely with both as they evaluate this matter and determine next steps,” said a spokesperson for Alaska Airlines, which also does not fly aircraft with the new software.
Shares of Boeing finished at US$184.39 (RM753), down 6.9 per cent. — AFP
a78b2cbaf30ddb55: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad wants the national healthcare transformation agenda, including modernising the system and improving patient service delivery, to be completed within the 15th parliamentary term.
He said the Ministry of Health (MOH) faces a major challenge of not only keeping facilities ready but also ensuring healthcare delivery consistently meets the people’s needs.
The focus, he said, includes streamlining existing systems and improving healthcare delivery, with patient experience and journey among the key considerations in executing the ministry’s initiatives.

“Faced with various challenges in healthcare services and the service system, I am certainly among the ministers dealing with a plethora of problems. Our ministry is, by nature, first, facility-based, and second, service-based.

“As such, the challenge for me, my ministry, MOH secretary-general Datuk Seri Hasnol Zam Zam Ahmad, and Health director-general, Datuk Dr Mahathar Abd Wahab, is to ensure that in this 15th Parliament, I fulfil my ambition of building a modern healthcare system and delivery.
“Whatever the method, platform or initiative, I will deliver it as soon as possible,” he said at the launch of the Financing for the Medicine-by-Post Initiative (UMP) today.
Also present were Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, his deputy Teo Nie Ching, and Ministry of Communications secretary-general, Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah.
Dzulkefly said MOH faces increasingly complex challenges, including food safety and quality, mental health and planetary health.

To strengthen healthcare transformation, he said, the Ministry is also focusing on digitalisation and interoperability across health systems and facilities, including electronic medical records that let public and private facilities share data.
Dzulkefly added that MOH wants healthcare delivery closer to the community and less dependent on hospitals or health facilities for matters that can be handled through alternatives.
He cited UMP as an example that allows patients to obtain follow-up medication without visiting a health facility solely to collect medicine.
“This is the patient experience. We want better treatment and, ultimately, less congestion at hospitals,” he said.
Dzulkefly said efforts to improve follow-up medicine delivery are nothing new, with pharmacy initiatives rolled out in phases over the past decade.

These include Drive-Through Pharmacy, Locker4U and the Local Follow-Up Medicine Supply Centre, as well as UMP and the MyUbat app, to ease the management of follow-up supplies and save patients time and money.
“Healthcare services must not only be available but easily accessible to all Malaysians. That is why we want to deliver on this. That is the mission of the year,” he said. — Bernama
41c5fda538188469: PUTRAJAYA: Members of the public continued to gather at Pusara Negara in Precinct 20 today to pay their last respects to Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali, wife of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad.
Dr Siti Hasmah died yesterday at the National Heart Institute (IJN), aged 100.
Flight attendant Mohamad Nur Firdaus Mansor, 41, from Seri Kembangan, recalled his time serving as a special officer to the family and his interactions with Dr Siti Hasmah.
He said that during the three to six months he spent serving the family in Langkawi, he had the opportunity to interact closely with Dr Siti Hasmah, whom he described as warm and motherly.
"When talking to her, she shared many views and offered advice like a mother, especially about daily life," he said when met at Pusara Negara today.
Firdaus said he received news of her death while on duty in China and went straight to her grave after landing at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) early this morning.
A steady stream of visitors arrived at the site to recite verses from the Quran and offer prayers under tents prepared for mourners.
Senior citizen Che Ah Mahat, 77, from Taman Dengkil Jaya, said she came with a friend to pay her last respects.
She said that although she knew Dr Siti Hasmah primarily as the wife of a former prime minister, she had always regarded her as a kind and gentle person.
Born on July 12, 1926, Dr Siti Hasmah was a prominent Malaysian figure who made significant contributions to medicine and social welfare beyond her role as the wife of a former prime minister.
She also made history as the first Malay woman to be offered admission to study medicine at the King Edward VII College of Medicine in Singapore.
c7301c87d80834c5: DUBLIN, Sept 29 — A New York Times technology executive was shot dead at a California sports complex on Saturday, with his wife’s parents arrested in connection with the killing.

Jonathan McKinsey, 40, was found at the Dublin Sports Grounds after the shooting at about 3pm, with the New York Post reporting that his in-laws, Shouyong Zhang and Shili Chen, both 77, were subsequently booked into Alameda County’s Santa Rita Jail.
A New York Times spokesman confirmed McKinsey was the victim and said he had been with the newspaper since 2023.

The couple are being held on suspicion of murder, while Alameda County Sheriff’s Office booking records list additional allegations including first-degree murder, felony conspiracy, unlawfully firing a gun and child endangerment involving a risk of serious injury or death.
McKinsey was married to Zhang and Chen’s daughter, Candice Jang, while the couple are based in the Dublin area and also have links to Albuquerque, New Mexico, according to the Post.
Zhang is listed in jail records as 5 feet 8 inches tall and weighing 165 pounds, while Chen is listed as 5 feet 2 inches and 110 pounds.

McKinsey joined The New York Times in 2023 after almost two decades in the technology industry, having previously held positions at Nasa’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Oracle, Coursera, UKG and Splunk.
At the Times, he initially worked as a senior engineering manager for the games platform before moving into games player experience.
He was promoted to director of engineering for games player experience in late 2025, leading a 25-member team working on features and monetisation for the newspaper’s puzzle games.
McKinsey earned a master’s degree in computer science from the University of California, Berkeley, in 2015.
A former Berkeley colleague, Nathan Wu, who said on LinkedIn that he had worked at the university, paid tribute to McKinsey on Sunday, writing: “Rip buddy.”
18015a9ae0d9dcdf: WASHINGTON: Meta launched a new business unit on Monday that will provide artificial intelligence (AI) services to enterprises, reported German Press Agency (dpa).
Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg said the company believed that "superintelligence will create significant new opportunities" for people and businesses.

"Meta already serves billions of people at scale and helps hundreds of millions of businesses reach customers. Today we are starting the next major pillar of our business, Meta Enterprise Platform, to help businesses use AI to grow and transform in new ways as well."
Meta Enterprise Platform will be headed by Chirantan Desai, who will report directly to Zuckerberg, the social media giant said.
Desai brings extensive experience in building full-stack software solutions, with particular expertise in AI, infrastructure, business applications and security, Meta said.
Most recently, Desai served as president and chief executive of MongoDB, a database software company.
Prior to that role, he led product and engineering at Cloudflare, a web infrastructure and security firm.
Desai also spent nearly eight years at ServiceNow, including a tenure as president and chief operating officer.
"Meta Enterprise Platform will focus on turning its AI stack into products and services that companies can deploy for their own businesses," Desai said.
"Our goal is to make Meta the place enterprises come to scale their businesses."
ff211cb6d1b2d647: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Three DAP lawmakers have welcomed the launch of the National Suicide and Fatal Injury Registry Malaysia (NSFIRM) and the Ministry of Health’s Postvention Services Guidelines, while calling for stronger crisis helpline standards.

In a joint statement, Bandar Kuching MP Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen and state assemblymen Lim Yi Wei (Kampung Tunku) and Michelle Ng Mei Sze (Subang Jaya) said the launch, three years after attempted suicide was decriminalised, reaffirms the government’s commitment to mental health.

They said that Malaysia previously lacked a systematic registry of suicide deaths and attempts. Suspected suicides may initially be classified as “sudden death”, and differences in reporting and investigation practices, along with stigma, have obscured the full picture.
“NSFIRM can make this picture clearer through systematic analysis and incident trend monitoring.

“In the age of social media, incident trend monitoring is crucial. Viral trends can become a vehicle for self-harm among vulnerable individuals, especially youth who lack safe spaces to express emotional distress, such as the TikTok ‘barcode’ trend,” they said.

They also welcomed commitments by major media players at the June 8 ministerial dialogue on ethical suicide reporting, including listing helplines. However, they cautioned that “many helplines mean little if nobody picks up the phone”.

They urged the Health Ministry, through the National Centre of Excellence for Mental Health, to implement performance indicators for helplines such as Talian Kasih 15999, Talian HEAL 15555 and Befrienders. These include answer and abandonment rates, waiting times, staffing across shifts and multilingual availability.

The trio also called for the guidelines to be coordinated with proposed civil service mental health guidelines, ensuring first responders are trained to record data and receive psychosocial support themselves.

38479c38cd1c8a85: KUALA LUMPUR: Consumer sentiment is expected to recover over the coming quarters as domestic pressures affecting household confidence have eased, said Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB).

The firm said Oppotus' Malaysian Consumer Confidence Index (MYCI) fell about nine per cent quarter-on-quarter to 123 points in the second quarter of 2026 (Q2 2026), its lowest reading since Q4 2022, with intent to make major purchases hitting the hardest.
However, gross domestic product grew six per cent year-on-year (YoY) in the same quarter, while private consumption expanded 4.8 per cent. Retail trade also grew 6.4 per cent in July.

"We read the disconnect as a hit to confidence that has changed the mix of spending rather than its level, with e-wallet use steady at groceries and convenience stores, while discretionary categories such as food delivery, hotels and flights declined," HLIB said in a note.

HLIB said it expects sentiment to improve as domestic pressures have eased, with the April Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) quota cut reversed from Sept 1 and headline inflation remaining below its 2.0 per cent peak in May.
"The only trigger that persists is the Iran war, but its cost is largely absorbed by the fiscal balance rather than households, with the RON95 price held at RM1.99 per litre," it added.

Meanwhile, HLIB said the MYCI does not necessarily reflect actual spending, noting that while the index stood at 141 in Q4 calendar year 2024 (CY24), YoY retail trade growth averaged 6.1 per cent, compared with 6.7 per cent in Q2 CY26 when the index was 18 points lower.

"Third, there is a direct precedent. MYCI slid 12 per cent to 124 by Q2 CY25 on US tariff announcements and the expanded sales and services tax but subsequently rebounded 9.7 per cent to 136 the following quarter, which also coincided with the RM100 Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) credit – it held around this level through Q1 CY26.
"With the fuel quota restored and another Sara credit possible under the 2027 budget, we expect sentiment to recover over the coming quarters," it added.
Additionally, HLIB expects the 2027 Budget to include a minimum wage revision, as the law requires a review at least every two years and the current RM1,700 rate took effect in February 2025.
Based on previous increases of RM100 to RM300, it expects the minimum wage to rise to RM1,900 to RM2,000 a month in 2027.

"Retailers will absorb an initial cost step-up, but we see the medium-term effect as net positive as higher pay at the bottom of the income bracket – where the propensity to consume is highest – flows back into value retailers such as 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd and Mr DIY Group (M) Bhd," it added.

0939e94412713470: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Perak PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul Amir Sabri today took his oath of office as a Senator representing the state for a three-year term from Sept 10, 2026 to Sept 9, 2029.

e8ed82f6c62af6cf: NEW YORK, Sept 29 — US prosecutors reopened an investigation Monday into an alleged gang rape at Cornell University following claims the elite college failed to properly punish the men involved.
The alleged victim said in a civil lawsuit this month she was drugged with ketamine, assaulted and raped in 2024 by seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity, a social club for male students.
Cornell closed the fraternity and temporarily suspended the students involved, several of whom were later expelled.
The newly-released details of the alleged incident have fuelled allegations that the university was too lenient and reignited a debate over sexual assault on US campuses.
Matthew Van Houten, district attorney for Tompkins County in New York, said that he plans to file criminal charges against the seven men.
He said his office chose in 2024 not to prosecute because the victim’s testimony did not establish a lack of consent, but had now decided to do so in light of her latest allegations.
“I recognise the reality that it can take years of therapy and healing for victims of sexual assaults to fully process and understand what happened to them,” Van Houten said in a statement.
“Seeking justice sometimes requires us to reconsider or reopen cases when we are provided with additional evidence.”
Kyle Kimball, vice president of university relations at Cornell, said the Ivy League school supports the decision to reinvestigate the case.
He also rejected a claim, made in the civil lawsuit, that the suspects were offered the opportunity to write essays to mitigate their conduct.
“Any suggestion that the university did not impose consequential punishments for those involved is false,” Kimball said.
The 101-page civil lawsuit filed in New York gives graphic details on the alleged assault of the woman, whose identity is being protected.
Notably, it provides a screenshot of a Snapchat group message advertising “free p**sy” during the incident, apparently an invitation for other fraternity members to take part.
The suit seeks financial damages from Cornell and the seven suspects, adding that the woman has suffered “severe emotional and psychological distress.”
British actor Florence Pugh has voiced her anger about the case, saying she felt “uneasy and sick and anxious” after hearing about it.
“Colleges/schools/universities repeatedly fail women around the world,” she wrote on Instagram.
“You build men that get taught through time and time again that they can do extreme harm and that they won’t be harmed in return,” Pugh said.
Prominent Democratic lawmaker Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez condemned a “culture of rape” at elite institutions like Cornell.
“Jane Doe, that survivor, lost her education because you can’t stay in school when something like that happens to you,” Ocasio-Cortez said Sunday.
“She had to lose her education, and those men were protected by an institution and granted an Ivy League degree as a reward. Never again.” — AFP
152184677a76fc2e: KUALA LUMPUR: Former national men's hockey captain Mirnawan Nawawi believes the Speedy Tigers have what it takes to reach the Asian Games final in Aichi-Nagoya.

"Malaysia's defence also needs to be wary of Korea's' penalty corner set-pieces. It will be great to see Malaysia qualify for the final after an outstanding performance in the group stage," said Mirnawan.
Malaysia edged Korea 2-1 in their last meeting at the Nations Cup in Cape Town, South Africa, in June.
However, the Koreans beat Malaysia 4-3 at the Sultan Azlan Shah Cup in Ipoh last November.
Malaysia reached the Asian Games final in 2010 (Guangzhou) and 2018 (Indonesia), finishing runners-up on both occasions.
The gold medallists will gain an automatic berth for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

443791d7383b0cd4: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — The Transport Ministry will assume sole authority for approving bunkering licences and related permits starting February 1, 2027.

Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said that centralising these approvals will provide operators with a single point of accountability and ensure more consistent decisions regarding safety, fuel quality, and environmental protection.
“I consider this as one of the major achievements by MOT because I have been minister of transport for a number of years.
“When we always talk about bunkering, we know that one of the key challenges and problems are the red tapes where a simple permit needs approval from multiple agencies and ministries.

This will help to boost our bunkering sector, hopefully,” Loke said while officiating Malaysia Maritime Week 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre.
This reform is part of a broader strategy to build a competitive bunkering sector capable of meeting modern shipping demands and preparing Malaysia for the transition to cleaner marine fuels.
Loke also revealed that the ministry is partnering with Australia to develop a policy and legal framework for green bunkering, focusing on fuels such as LNG, biofuels, and methanol.

“This work also supports a wider international commitment. In the International Maritime Organisation's 2023 Greenhouse Gas Strategy calls for zero or near-zero emission fuels and technologies to account for at least 5 per cent of the energy use by international shipping by 2030, with a target of 10 per cent.

6217e69177ab4624: SEPANG: Ticket sales for the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 at Sepang International Circuit (SIC) could hit 100,000, buoyed by an overwhelming response.

SIC chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif said about 95,000 three-day tickets had been sold ahead of the Oct 2 to 4 race weekend, a strong showing for F1's return to Malaysia after a nine-year absence.

Tickets for the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain GP in Malaysia 2026 are sold as three-day passes only; single-day tickets are not available.

Azhan also said international visitors accounted for 50 per cent of ticket sales, highlighting the race's strong appeal among overseas fans.
"We have seen from the ticket buyers that 50 per cent are from overseas. This is good for us. The more tourists come over and spend, the better it is for the economy," he said.
He said SIC was undergoing rapid transformation to meet Formula 1 requirements, singling out the paddock as one of the major areas upgraded ahead of the race.
Azhan said the operation's scale had posed a major logistical challenge, with Formula 1 cargo alone estimated at four to five times the volume SIC handles for MotoGP.
He was also impressed by Bahrain International Circuit's (BIC) entertainment line-up as part of the race experience, saying fans would certainly get added value beyond the on-track action.
"I've seen the list of entertainers that Bahrain has brought here, and I'm blown away. I'm pretty sure the people who have bought tickets will get their value back when they come here," he said.

The co-founder of both Swedish House Mafia and Axwell Λ Ingrosso joins an exciting line-up of race-weekend concerts, following the confirmation that multi-platinum-selling hitmaker Martin Garrix will headline the post-race concert on Sunday, Oct 4.

Sheikh Salman said his main hope was for the race to be run safely while giving fans a memorable experience that offers them a taste of Bahrain.
"I hope they see our culture, capture the memories and leave with a smile," he said.

In July, Formula 1 confirmed Malaysia as host of the Gulf Air Bahrain GP, following an agreement between Formula 1, the International Automobile Federation (FIA) and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
The agreement keeps the Bahrain GP on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race had been cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

4910f253ca247cc0: WASHINGTON, Sept 29 — President Donald Trump on Monday denied a report by the news outlet Axios that he offered Iran sanctions relief and the release of frozen funds, as the Mideast war drags on.
“Axios just released a story that ‘Trump’ offered Sanctions Relief and Frozen Funds to Iran. This is untrue. I offered them NOTHING!,” Trump said on his Truth Social platform.

On Sunday, Trump told Axios he expected talks to resume in coming days.
The strategic Strait of Hormuz lies at the heart of the conflict. The narrow waterway normally carries a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied gas.
The route has been effectively blockaded by Tehran since the war began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28.

Prices for gas and other products in the US have risen dramatically since the war began, as Trump faces dwindling popularity in national polls and his party worries about losing their majority in Congress in midterm elections come November. — AFP
c688978a6d7d29cf: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — With Malaysia expected to be an aged nation by 2048, the focus should not only be on ensuring sufficient retirement savings but also ensuring people have the choice to work past age 60, the prime minister said today.
In Malaysia, the minimum retirement age for the private sector and the mandatory retirement age for civil servants are both currently at age 60.

In his speech, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said those who want to work after age 60 should be given the choice, but did not say whether there are plans to raise the minimum or mandatory retirement age.
“Raising the floor is only half the work. We must also raise the ceiling by ensuring that longer lives are lived with agency, connection and purpose.

“Those who are capable and wish to continue working beyond 60 should have the opportunity to do so. This is about choice, not compulsion,” he said in his speech at the International Social Wellbeing Conference 2026 here, which was read out on his behalf by Minister of Finance II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
Anwar’s raising the floor remark alludes to his earlier comments in his speech, including having adequate savings and sustainable income for retirement.

Anwar pointed out that allowing work beyond 60 or such age-friendly employment can “retain experience, strengthen organisations and allow people to remain economically active on terms that respect their circumstances.”
Anwar said older people can still give valuable contributions to society, even if these may not appear in economic statistics.
“Experience, judgment and accumulated knowledge remain valuable assets to society,” he said.
He gave examples such as a retired teacher who mentors students, a grandparent supporting a working family, and a community leader who helps strengthen social cohesion.

“We must raise the floor so that every Malaysian can age with dignity and security. We must also raise the ceiling so that longer lives remain years of purpose, contribution and connection. And we must shorten the distance between policy and delivery,” he said in concluding his speech.
Earlier in his speech, Anwar said Malaysians are living longer, and the key question for the country is how to ensure longer lives are lived with dignity, financial security, good health and purpose.

bfa0244ddaa97fc0: PETALING JAYA: Ismail Lasim should stay on as menteri besar of Negeri Sembilan despite several political missteps barely two months into his tenure, analysts say.

0401fe10b3735d43: PETALING JAYA: Adun Juasseh Ismail Lasim wajar kekal sebagai menteri besar Negeri Sembilan walaupun beberapa tindakannya mengundang kontroversi, tidak sampai dua bulan selepas memegang jawatan itu, kata penganalisis.

Azmi Hassan dari Akademi Nusantara berkata Ismail masih mempunyai sokongan kuat dalam kalangan akar umbi, manakala penganalisis politik Mazlan Ali berpandangan Umno akan berdepan kesukaran untuk mencari penggantinya.

Menurutnya, kesilapan Ismail dalam menangani pertikaian membabitkan kedudukan Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, setakat ini tidak menjejaskan sokongan politik terhadapnya.
“Keputusan yang perlu dibuat Ismail sangat sukar kerana ia menyentuh soal institusi diraja dan istana,” katanya kepada FMT.
Menurutnya, walaupun Ismail tidak begitu dikenali di peringkat nasional, beliau masih mempunyai pengaruh kuat dalam kalangan akar umbi Negeri Sembilan, khususnya di Kuala Pilah.
Ismail merupakan Adun tujuh penggal, bermula di Senaling sebelum mewakili Juasseh, yang menurut Azmi menunjukkan beliau mempunyai asas sokongan tempatan yang kukuh.
Sebelum ini, kumpulan bekas penjawat awam kanan G25 menggesa Ismail meletak jawatan sebagai menteri besar susulan cara beliau menangani krisis membabitkan istana.

Kumpulan itu berkata kedudukan Ismail tidak lagi dapat dipertahankan selepas beliau menandatangani satu proklamasi yang mahu Tuanku Muhriz disingkirkan, sebelum memberikan penjelasan yang bercanggah mengenai dokumen berkenaan.

Azmi berkata tanggapan Ismail bukan pilihan utama Umno untuk menjadi menteri besar timbul kerana Ketua Umno Negeri Sembilan Jalaluddin Alias sebelum ini dilihat sebagai calon utama bagi jawatan tersebut.

Jalaluddin mengetuai tindakan 14 Adun Umno menarik sokongan terhadap menteri besar ketika itu, Aminuddin Harun, menjelang PRN pada 1 Ogos, menyebabkan ramai menjangkakan beliau akan mengambil alih jawatan berkenaan.
Bagaimanapun, Azmi berkata Ismail kini dilihat mempunyai sokongan mencukupi dalam kalangan akar umbi dan kepimpinan Umno untuk terus mengetuai pentadbiran negeri di bawah parti itu.
Mazlan pula berkata walaupun kenyataan bercanggah Ismail mengenai proklamasi berkenaan boleh dianggap sebagai kesilapan serius, usaha menggantikannya sebagai menteri besar bukan sesuatu yang mudah.
Katanya, ada pandangan Jalaluddin bukan pilihan Tuanku Muhriz untuk jawatan menteri besar walaupun sebelum ini dianggap calon utama.
Selain itu, katanya, Umno juga mungkin berdepan kesukaran mencari calon menteri besar dan barisan exco baharu yang boleh diterima pemerintah negeri.
010ffd0f5843541c: PETALING JAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has arrested a former senior management officer of a corporation on suspicion of abusing his power in making operating expense payments totalling approximately RM42 million to several companies.
A source said the man in his 50s was arrested at about 1pm yesterday at his residence in the Klang Valley.

"Preliminary investigations found that the suspect allegedly committed the offences in 2017, making payments related to operating expenses to several companies that the suspect is believed to have interests in," said the source.
The arrest follows an MACC investigation into losses suffered by UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd in 2023.
MACC chief commissioner Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrest when contacted and said the case is being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009 for the abuse of power.
He previously said that the issues under investigation in the UiTM Holdings probe included a RM42 million payment linked to a 50MW solar project in Gambang, Pahang.
He said the money was allegedly used for purposes unrelated to the solar project, and the payment was made without the approval of the UiTM Holdings board.
The suspect is expected to be charged in court on Thursday.
4d4e4e36bb97ed86: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia aims to raise its port handling capacity to 100 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) by 2035 as it strengthens its position as a global maritime and logistics hub.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the target would be pursued through a new port on Carey Island and the Westports 2 expansion at Port Klang.
"It would also include Phases 3 and 4 of the Port of Tanjung Pelepas development, as well as expansions at Kuantan and Kemaman ports," he said in his speech at the 2026 Malaysia Maritime Week.
Also present were Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah and Transport Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Jana Santhiran Muniayan.
Loke said Port Klang retained its position as the world's 10th-busiest container port in the latest Lloyd's List One Hundred Container Ports 2026 ranking.
It handled 15,138,772 TEUs in 2025, up from 14,644,527 TEUs in 2024, an increase of 3.4 per cent.
The Port of Johor followed closely in 11th place, handling 15,110,050 TEUs in 2025.
"Together, these achievements reflect the strength of Malaysia's ports and their growing contribution to global trade," he said.
Loke said expanding port capacity would also support the growth of Malaysia's shipping fleet and maritime industries.
"As we expand our ports, have more ships coming into our country and see more trade, we are also building up our Malaysian fleet.
"We are encouraging shipowners to build more ships under the Malaysian flag and have more Malaysian-flagged vessels.
"This is important from a strategic point of view and for national security," he said.
Loke said the government was working with the Malaysian Shipowners' Association (Masa) to encourage the construction of more Malaysian-flagged vessels.
"This will also create an industry in itself. We will continue to drive the development of the shipbuilding industry, with more shipyards, more shipbuilding and more ship repair.
"So, these are all very important jobs to be created under our maritime sector," he said.

ccb703928cef4673: NAGOYA: Thailand's greater hunger for victory, coupled with their consistency in attack and defence, proved the difference as Malaysia missed out on the men's regu sepak takraw gold medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games today.
National coach Ahmad Jais Baharun said Thailand produced the more composed performance throughout the final, making it difficult for Malaysia to find their rhythm and shift the momentum.

2b5aaf87001d69e4: AI promises to deliver significant productivity gains to individuals and businesses, but could it also help developed market governments reduce their budget deficits and pay down debt? It might.

The estimated productivity gains from AI are highly uncertain. Chicago Federal Reserve Board economist Ezra Karger and his colleagues recently surveyed economists, superforecasters, AI experts, and the general public on the question.
The median estimate for the boost to US gross domestic product (GDP) growth from AI was around 0.5 percentage point per year through 2031.
Economists, perhaps unsurprisingly, are much more conservative than the other groups, expecting only a 0.1 percentage point boost annually over the next five years.
But one thing everyone can agree on is that if productivity increases, GDP growth will rise. This can happen through higher corporate profits as businesses reduce costs or increase output.
Or it could happen through higher real wages if workers become more productive, increasing their bargaining power and ability to demand better pay.
To put things simply, both businesses and workers pay taxes, which means that, all else being equal, increased productivity should indirectly lead to higher tax revenues for the government.
This, in turn, should reduce the budget deficit and the debt-to-GDP ratio, unless revenue increases are outpaced by increased government spending.
The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) currently projects that the US debt-to-GDP ratio will reach 120 per cent in 2036.

With a productivity boost of 0.5 percentage points per year – again, with all else being equal – this ratio could fall to under 111 per cent if all the benefits accrue to businesses and to below 110 per cent if half of the productivity gains are captured by workers.
That's all theory, however. In practice, the situation is a lot more complicated.
The bottom line is that AI productivity gains may be able to improve the fiscal outlook for the US, though likely not nearly enough to truly get the country out of its debt spiral.
The US is running chronically high deficits of more than five per cent and has one of the lowest effective corporate tax rates anywhere in the industrialised world.
The result is that – even in fairly optimistic scenarios – the benefits of the growth boost could remain largely with the private sector and do little to improve government finances.
However, in other countries with higher tax rates and smaller deficits, the AI productivity boost could be a real game changer.
Let's look at the UK, starting with the baseline projections from the UK Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) through 2031.
Because growth rates in Britain are lower than in the US, a productivity boost of 0.1 to 0.5 percentage points translates into a larger relative increase in profits and wages.
Tax rates in the UK are also higher than in the US, which means the government should capture a larger share of these gains.
The OBR currently estimates that the UK debt-to-GDP ratio will be 95 per cent in 2031.

Assuming an AI productivity boost similar to the one expected for the US, I estimate that this ratio could drop to about 89 per cent. This is a six-percentage-point decline in five years, roughly twice the reduction in the US over the same period.

The picture improves further for the taxpayer when examining the potential impact on projected budget deficits. By 2031, a 0.1 percentage point boost to UK GDP growth from AI could reduce the budget deficit by a full percentage point.
If the GDP boost from AI is instead at the higher end of the range, the budget deficit could shrink by up to 1.3 percentage points compared with current projections.
For a country forecast to run a deficit of less than three per cent of GDP in the late 2020s, this means it could halve its deficit if the benefits from AI come to pass.

One caveat is that the GDP boost from AI could be lower in the UK than in the US given that Britain has a less dynamic economy. And, of course, the problem with any such forecast is – as always – the word "if".
* Writing for Reuters, the writer is an investment strategist for Panmure Liberum

415f5d23602ccc06: PETALING JAYA: The Sarawak government has asked Putrajaya for more incentives and better infrastructure under Budget 2027 to attract investments in semiconductors, high-tech manufacturing and clean energy, among others.

The proposed incentives were among the key issues discussed at a meeting between Sarawak deputy premier Awang Tengah Ali Hasan, who is also the state’s international trade, industry and investment minister, and federal investment, trade and industry minister Johari Ghani in Putrajaya yesterday.

According to Dayak Daily, the Sarawak international trade, industry and investment ministry said the discussions explored opportunities to expand high-value and emerging industries such as advanced manufacturing, semiconductors and the digital economy.

Both sides highlighted the importance of ensuring that appropriate incentives, infrastructure, skilled talent and a supportive investment ecosystem are in place to facilitate new investments and the expansion of existing industries.
The meeting also covered Sarawak's development priorities under the state's 2030 post Covid-19 development strategy, as well as Malaysia's broader industrial and investment agenda.
These priorities include creating quality jobs, developing local talent, strengthening local enterprises and promoting technology adoption and innovation.
9f16bcd152714b4d: LOS ANGELES: Lindsay Lohan is joining forces with Malaysia-born British actor Henry Golding for an upcoming Netflix romantic drama titled Return To You.

The project marks a nostalgic reunion for Lohan, who will produce and star in the feature under the direction of Mark Waters—the filmmaker behind two of her most iconic career hits, Mean Girls and Freaky Friday, Deadline reported.

Set in 2008, the film follows a high-powered yet isolated female lawyer, played by Lohan, who accidentally comes into possession of a deeply emotional DVD intended for a grieving husband, portrayed by Golding. Guided solely by the subtle clues contained within the recorded message, she embarks on a quest to track him down.

Screenwriter Eric Champnella penned the script, while Brad Krevoy, who previously collaborated with Lohan on her popular Netflix holiday titles Falling for Christmas and Irish Wish, is onboard to produce.
Both leads have carved out formidable reputations within the romance genre.

Golding previously charmed audiences as the male lead in the global box-office phenomenon Crazy Rich Asians and the festive hit Last Christmas, alongside recent roles in Persuasion and Daniela Forever.
Lohan, who recently reprised her famous role in the 2025 sequel Freakier Friday, continues her successful creative partnership with Netflix following a string of hit romantic comedies.
07dda051ff3daba3: HONG KONG: Shares in Chinese fast-fashion giant Shein plunged more than 11% in Hong Kong on Tuesday after releasing disappointing financial results.

The company has faced scrutiny over its environmental footprint and allegations of human rights violations and faces growing competition from low-cost e-commerce companies such as Temu and AliExpress.
The firm said on Monday that revenue grew just 1% on-year in the first six months of the year, while its operating profit halved.
By around lunch on Tuesday, Shein's share price had pared some of the losses but was still down 10.9% at HK$31.44.

Monday's results were Shein's first since its high-profile initial public offering this month, which put the company's valuation at around US$26.3 billion – well short of the nearly $100 billion during private fundraising rounds in 2022.
Net revenue from Europe fell 13.9% to nearly US$3.8 billion for the second quarter, Shein reported.
The decrease "reflects a decline in sales volume as we raised prices and lowered online advertising spending" in anticipation of the removal of the customs duty exemption, the company said.
Another key market, the US, saw revenue drop 6% in April-June, reflecting the impact of tariffs.
Since its first day of trading on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in September, Shein's share price has fallen more than 35%.

The accelerating decline in Shein's operating profit "clouds the extent of a 2027 recovery from freight relief and an unproven push into higher-priced brands", said Catherine Lim, an analyst at Business Intelligence.

"Management plans to absorb freight and tariff costs rather than raise prices to protect the company's competitive position," she said, adding that localising stock in Europe will lead to higher logistics costs in the short term.
4060a42870d712dc: KUALA LUMPUR: Setiausaha Agung DAP Loke Siew Fook berkata peletakan jawatannya sebagai menteri pengangkutan hanya akan berkuat kuasa sebaik sahaja bekas perdana menteri Najib Razak dibebaskan dari penjara untuk menjalani baki hukuman di bawah tahanan rumah.

“Beliau (Anwar) menasihati saya untuk meneruskan tugas buat sementara waktu. Beliau akan membuat keputusan, tetapi saya katakan bahawa perlu juga ada satu tempoh masa.

Umno melancarkan kutipan dana bagi membantu Najib membayar denda itu sejurus selepas pengampunan tersebut diumumkan, dan telah mengumpulkan RM9.25 juta setakat Ahad.
05075752abd85a04: LETTERS: Under the Budi95 system, eligible citizens receive subsidised RON95 petrol at RM 1.99 per litre, subject to a monthly quota of 300 litres.
Budi95 is a subsidy rationalisation programme with the primary goal of easing the subsidy burden on the government's fiscal policy.

Research has proved that an increase in fuel prices will lead to a transmission in the price level, especially in Malaysia, as our Consumer Price Index focuses on the food and beverages and transportation baskets.
These two baskets are linked to the fuel price. Consequently, while targeted mechanisms like Budi95 reduce inflationary pressures, they do not resolve long-run price vulnerabilities.

Escalating geopolitical tensions between the United States and Iran have disrupted global crude oil supply, driving market prices above US$100 per barrel. According to the Ministry of Finance, Budi95 spent RM3 billion and RM5 billion during March and May 2026, respectively.

Compared with the pre-crisis baseline of RM0.7 billion in January 2026, monthly subsidy spending surged between 300 and 600 per cent. This huge expenditure forced the government to cut the budget for other development purposes.
To build long-term economic resilience, Malaysia must move beyond temporary fuel subsidies and consider two primary strategies:

Firstly, we should start research and development on biofuel products. Thailand has already mainstreamed the usage of biofuel "Gasohol", while Indonesia has started to introduce bio-gasoline - Pertamax Green E5.

As one of the world's leading palm oil producers, Malaysia possesses a distinct comparative advantage in feedstock availability. Mainstreaming domestic biofuels would mitigate our reliance on crude oil import benchmarks and buffer local pump prices against global geopolitical shocks.
Secondly, the government should continue to rationalise the subsidy system. Although we have Budi-95 for now, it is not enough for the long term, as it is limited in quantity.
The government needs to address the difference between the global fuel price and subsidised retail price. It will increase the government's fiscal burden amid fluctuations in the global fuel price.

However, rather than introducing subsidised fuel with limited quantity, the government should introduce a system like Sumbangan Asas Rahmah to give direct cash assistance for petrol in a one-off and fixed amount to eligible users, such as B40 and M40 households, to reduce the petrol price burden on the cost of living among households.
Therefore, it will ease the government's subsidy system and fiscal burden.

Budi95 serves as an effective short-term shield against energy price shocks, but it is fiscally unsustainable over the long run. To secure future fiscal stability and economic resilience, we must pivot towards structural biofuel integration and direct income support.
School of Economics, Finance and Banking,
8ee07c2a8f075a06: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget will address the challenges of an ageing population alongside cost-of-living pressures and the need for better-quality jobs, Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said.
He said the needs of Malaysians living longer would be considered as part of the government's broader efforts to raise incomes and improve living standards.
"As we are addressing those issues, we will take the needs of a longer-living Malaysian, living better quality lives, as part and parcel of things that we address in Malaysia," he said.
Amir was speaking to reporters after the Employees Provident Fund's (EPF) International Social Wellbeing Conference 2026 here on Tuesday.
He said the government was finalising the 2027 Budget, scheduled to be tabled on Oct 9, with cost of living, better-quality jobs and efforts to lift lower-income groups among its key priorities.
Strengthening retirement adequacy would also require Malaysians to take a more active role in building their savings, he said.
"The key now is actually to continue that drive to increase the contributions into the fund, so that in a sense we will have an adequate savings for Malaysians," he said.
Amir said the EPF was introducing mechanisms to help members make their savings last longer, including regular withdrawals instead of lump-sum payments.
Its Retirement Income Adequacy (Ria) framework provides different savings benchmarks to help members plan according to their desired retirement lifestyle.
The framework also includes an automatic adjustment mechanism to account for inflation and changes in the cost of living.
"If the basic savings stays the same for 20 years, you know the basic savings is not going to be enough," he said.

Amir said the government supported the EPF's efforts to strengthen retirement savings and encouraged it to continue introducing measures that give members greater flexibility in managing their retirement income.
Beyond retirement savings, he said government-linked investment companies (GLICs) and government-linked companies (GLCs) were helping to create better-quality jobs and raise incomes.
More than 92 per cent of GLCs under the GLICs have adopted a living wage since the beginning of this year, moving beyond the statutory minimum wage.
The move is intended to set a higher wage benchmark and encourage the private sector to offer better pay as productivity improves.

Amir said GLICs were also supporting talent development through programmes such as Bakat Madani, which connects university and technical and vocational education and training (TVET) graduates with internship and training opportunities.
About 25,000 individuals are expected to benefit from the programme this year and next.
He added that GLIC investments were increasingly aligned with the needs of an ageing population, including investments in companies providing care services and retirement villages.
c5563a36c4d193dc: PUTRAJAYA: The public, particularly senior citizens, have been reminded not to fall victim to scams involving registration for the free Medicines By Post programme starting Oct 1.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said registration for the programme was free and could only be done through Health Ministry facilities.
"Medicines By Post registration is through Health Ministry facilities. It is not through any TikTok or Facebook accounts.
"There is no registration process other than through the ministry itself," he told reporters after attending the launch of the Medicines By Post financing initiative at the Communications Ministry.
Fahmi said the public should not pay anyone offering to register them for the programme through unofficial channels.

He said the initiative would cover delivery costs for Malaysians enrolled in Medicines By Post nationwide from Oct 1, with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) covering the delivery charges and Pos Malaysia handling the service.
Previously, patients had to pay RM5.70 for deliveries in Peninsular Malaysia and RM12.50 for Sabah and Sarawak.

Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the initiative would particularly benefit patients in rural and remote areas by allowing them to receive their medicines without having to travel to health facilities solely for collection.
"Patients, especially those in rural and remote areas, no longer need to travel just to collect their medicines.
"This saves them time and travel costs, while making it more convenient for them to receive their medicines," he said.
Dzulkefly said the initiative would also improve the patient experience by making medicine collection more convenient and reducing the need for patients to queue at health facilities.
"At the same time, it can help reduce congestion and the burden on hospitals and health facilities, allowing healthcare services to be delivered more efficiently," he said.
The Medicines By Post programme, introduced in 2011, is expected to benefit about 87,000 registered patients annually.
Dzulkefly said the initiative reflected the government's efforts to make healthcare services more accessible, particularly for patients who face difficulties travelling to health facilities.
The public have also been urged to register for the service through Health Ministry facilities and the MyUBAT system, rather than through social media platforms or unofficial links.
MyUBAT provides users with access to medicine supply services and allows them to monitor the status of Medicines
b5d7c95660dfc9a9: WASHINGTON: A new US import ban on several Canadian products, including many alcoholic beverages, went into effect Tuesday as US President Donald Trump's economic war against one of his country's largest trading partners deepens.
The ban was announced earlier this month and entered into force on Tuesday at 12:01 am US Eastern time.
It comes as the neighbouring nations have been locked in a cycle of spiralling trade tensions after talks to resolve the crisis broke down in August after days of meetings in Washington.
Since taking office for his second term, Trump has upended global trade by applying a slew of sometimes eyewateringly high tariffs on friends and foes alike.
The new import ban includes an array of alcoholic beverages, including beer, sparkling wine, brandy, sake and many types of liquor.
It also covers the dairy-based whey protein as well as high-powered motorcycles.
Trump announced the latest measures on Sept 8, after Canada imposed retaliatory tariffs applying to around US$20 billion in US exports.
The US president has justified the ban on Canadian alcohol products by pointing towards "discriminatory" boycotts and tariffs on US products of the same nature.
On Monday, he accused his country's second-largest trading partner of being "entitled".
"The problem is that they've treated the US very unfairly. They have been one of the worst countries in the entire world," he told reporters at the White House.
Anti-US sentiment has been high in Canada since Trump took office, with the billionaire frequently referring to the country of 41.7 million people as the United States' "51st state".
In August, Trump signed an executive order to rename Lake Ontario, on the border with Canada, to "Lake America".
The move sparked fury in Canada amid the broad wave of patriotism brought on by Trump's hostility.

Although Carney is backed by Canadian public opinion, his country remains reliant on its southern neighbour. Nearly 60% of Canada's imports come from the US, and about 70% of its exports go to the US market.
To help businesses and workers, Canada's government has unveiled an aid package worth US$5.4 billion.
Still, the impact of Tuesday's import ban could be "significant", said Spirits Canada, a trade association for the country's alcohol sector.
The US is by far Canada's most important export market for spirits, with about 50% of Canadian spirits production tied to US demand.
"This leaves Canadian producers with limited ability to replace lost US demand in the near term," said the association.
971378e33c9b717f: SHAH ALAM: Seramai 50 penduduk Taman Sri Muda memenangi saman terhadap kerajaan dan agensi lain atas kecuaian serta pelanggaran tanggungjawab berkait banjir pada 2021 yang meragut 12 nyawa di kawasan itu.

Di Mahkamah Tinggi Shah Alam hari ini, Pesuruhjaya Kehakiman Shoba Rajah berkata penduduk berkenaan berjaya membuktikan tuntutan mereka berdasarkan imbangan kebarangkalian terhadap kerajaan dan dua agensi negeri.

“Mahkamah memutuskan bahawa plaintif berjaya membuktikan kewujudan kewajipan berjaga-jaga yang boleh dijangka, yang timbul daripada fungsi operasi dan tanggungjawab pengurusan bencana defendan (kerajaan).

“Pembelaan ‘takdir Tuhan’ yang dikemukakan tidak terpakai apabila campur tangan manusia yang munasabah boleh dilakukan. Kecuaian telah dibuktikan. Doktrin kekebalan asing tidak relevan di bawah undang-undang Malaysia,” katanya.

Mahkamah berkata Agensi Pengurusan Bencana Negara 'gagal meningkatkan tahap tindak balas bencana, mengekalkan pusat penyelarasan utama dan mengerahkan Pasukan Mencari dan Menyelamat Khas Malaysia (SMART) dengan berkesan' semasa banjir itu.
“Pihak berkuasa gagal menguruskan lokasi kejadian dengan berkesan, menyebabkan usaha mencari dan menyelamat sebahagian besarnya diserahkan kepada NGO dan anggota masyarakat setempat,” kata Shoba.
Beliau turut berkata Jabatan Meteorologi gagal mengeluarkan amaran tepat pada masanya pada tahap bahaya yang sewajarnya, meskipun ramalannya menunjukkan bahawa ambang yang berkaitan telah dicapai.
Mahkamah memutuskan Jabatan Pengairan dan Saliran (JPS) Selangor dan Majlis Bandaraya Shah Alam (MBSA) bertanggungan secara bersama dengan kerajaan Persekutuan.
